{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-id-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"d9f465cd814e3cdcbe56c40d641969f2b5d11bd2c52003f2431e5d798dc1905a","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-id-class-d:lineage:63","source_registry_sha256":"9c432577e712960022ff656d6738a091319c6e5e4dcbdcf9429cd450e142e543","source_liveness_sha256":"eee60602368bd429216c9c2833be0be6ed9e505e5c5accebaefb9d2b9a847475"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Vehicle emergencies and crash responsibilities","heading":"C — Vehicle emergencies and crash responsibilities","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Vehicle emergencies and crash responsibilities

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A115
Prepare for hazards and think before reacting, since an instinctive hard-brake response during a skid can be inappropriate. [A115]
Source: [A115 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A115
On slick roads, slow before a stop and avoid braking hard enough to lock the wheels. [A115]
Source: [A115 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A115
Skids can occur on ice, packed snow or wet pavement, and also on dry pavement during high-speed travel or abrupt stops. [A115]
Source: [A115 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A116
For the described rear-wheel skid, release the accelerator without hitting the brake and steer toward the rear wheels' slide. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A116
If the rear wheels slide right, the handbook's example directs the front wheels to the right. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A116
Before driving on snow or ice, practice stopping and skid recovery in a safe place, ideally private property. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A116
Read the vehicle's manual for its ABS operating instructions. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A116
During a hard emergency stop with ABS, hold continuous pedal pressure and do not pump the brake. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A116
ABS pulses the brakes automatically, so hard braking may produce pump noise and a noticeable pedal pulse. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A116
Normal ABS noise and pulsation are not reasons to lift the foot from the brake during the stop. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A117
For a quick stop without ABS, press firmly enough to stop promptly without locking the brakes. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A117
If non-ABS brakes lock and skidding begins, promptly ease off the pedal. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A117
After the non-ABS skid stops, reapply the brake and repeat release and reapplication if necessary until stopped. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A117
If a stalled car can be moved, pull it completely off the road and use emergency flashers. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A117
Raise the stalled vehicle's hood to indicate trouble. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A117
If unable to leave the road, stop where following traffic has a clear view, avoiding a spot just beyond a hill or around a curve. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A117
The breakdown guidance says to place available warning flares two hundred to three hundred feet behind the car. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A117
If no flares are available, the handbook advises warning traffic from the roadside with a white cloth or flag if available, while staying out of the roadway. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A118
Crash avoidance may involve a direction change by steering or a speed change by braking or accelerating. [A118]
Source: [A118 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A118
If stopping in time appears impossible, consider steering clear and, if possible, stay off the brakes during the turn to retain control. [A118]
Source: [A118 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A118
Acceleration may prevent or reduce an impact from a vehicle approaching from the side or rear. [A118]
Source: [A118 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A118
Fasten the safety belt correctly before travel as crash protection. [A118]
Source: [A118 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A119
If a head-on threat leaves time to react, slow and warn the other driver with lights and horn. [A119]
Source: [A119 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A119
For that head-on threat, move as far right as possible rather than left, because the other driver may recover. [A119]
Source: [A119 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A119
If the collision cannot be avoided, the handbook advises an angled impact instead of a direct head-on impact. [A119]
Source: [A119 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec14-F26 | anchor: A120
For a tire blowout, grip the wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight rather than braking abruptly. [A120]
Source: [A120 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F27 | anchor: A120
After a blowout, gradually release the accelerator and wait for complete control before braking. [A120]
Source: [A120 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F28 | anchor: A120
Once the blown-tire vehicle is controlled, brake gently and leave the roadway at the nearest safe place. [A120]
Source: [A120 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F29 | anchor: A120
If wheels leave the pavement, hold the wheel firmly, continue straight and remain on the shoulder when no immediate obstacle is present. [A120]
Source: [A120 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F30 | anchor: A120
After dropping off the pavement, release the accelerator and brake gently. [A120]
Source: [A120 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F31 | anchor: A120
After slowing off the pavement, find a traffic opening and return only when safe, avoiding an oversteer across the center line. [A120]
Source: [A120 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0120]

Misconceptions: Do not pump an ABS brake during a hard emergency stop. A departure from the pavement calls for control and a safe opening before reentry. Quick Clearance has explicit road and injury conditions.
Mnemonic: Control, warn and seek help is a teaching cue for the source-supported emergency sequence.
Glossary: ABS means anti-lock braking system; a blowout is sudden tire failure; Quick Clearance describes moving a qualifying crash vehicle out of travel lanes.
Dynamic facts: legal thresholds, department procedures and vehicle-specific emergency operation remain limited to the staged official text and declared review debt.
